result.title: Physical activity and incident type 2 diabetes in adults: a prospective cohort analysis of primary care records
result.authorString: Okafor NC, Lindqvist A, Ramirez JP, Tanaka H.
result.abstractText: Objective: To quantify the association between self-reported physical activity and incident type 2 diabetes in a large primary care cohort. Design: Prospective cohort analysis of routinely collected electronic health records. Setting: Nine primary care networks in Northern Europe. Participants: 214,806 adults aged 40 to 75 years without diabetes at baseline. Main outcome measures: Incident type 2 diabetes identified from diagnostic coding and prescription records. Results: Higher moderate-to-vigorous physical activity was associated with a lower hazard of incident diabetes (adjusted hazard ratio 0.72, 95% confidence interval 0.68 to 0.77, comparing the highest with the lowest quartile). Conclusions: Physical activity is associated with a substantially lower risk of incident type 2 diabetes, and the association persists after adjustment for body mass index.

result.title: Wearable-derived step counts and cardiometabolic risk markers: a cross-sectional study in community volunteers
result.authorString: Bauer M; Kowalski E; Chen LY
result.abstractText: Step counts recorded by consumer wearables were compared with cardiometabolic risk markers in 1,842 community volunteers. Higher daily step counts were associated with lower resting blood pressure and lower fasting glucose, but the associations attenuated after adjustment for self-reported physical activity.
